I'm an avid reader of the Dune series, both classic, and the nuDune, and am wondering if the users of /v/Dune would be interested in getting a read-along series of threads going. It would be a great way to add some content to the subverse, and allow us to share our opinions of various aspects of the books. Who else is game?

I'd like to lay out some ground rules to keep the conversation civil, and allow the greatest number of voaters to enjoy the ongoing conversation.

  1. No bullshit arguments about the classics vs. nuDune. It's dumb. That's the Dune equivalent of Kirk vs. Picard. It doesn't do a damn thing to add to the conversation, and just divides the community. If you like a book then you like a book, and if you don't then you don't. Leave the elitist tribalism for a forum that'll embrace it.
  2. One chapter per week. We all agree to read a specific portion of a book ahead of time, and then discuss that specific chapter. This may be a bit difficult due to the varying publications, but chapters can basically be divided into the collection of pages between the philosophical headers on different pages.
  3. We discuss not only the events of the pages, but the philosophical, cultural, and religious points raised by the author.

Does anyone else have any ground rules that should be laid down before we start?

One thing that I'd like to put up to a vote will be whether we read the books in story-chronological order, or in publishing order. Should we start with Dune, or The Butlerian Jihad?

Hi, just a short letter. I am a student who went to college outside the US. Why? Cheaper costs by far and my degree counts as a US degree. A professional school 4 years can be obtained for less than 20 k for all four years. Of course housing and food is not included but......that is a variable only you can determine. My rent was 150 US per month. The cost for books was significantly lower because the they do not sell the same "quality", paper is different and perhaps black and white photos...but the same editions and authors......and you cannot buy them in the US. It was a long hard road, I had no relatives or even language skills other than english. Most if not all accredited colleges teach in english! Would I do it again......? If you want the degree bad enough you will...... There are countries , Germany that you can even attend for free. I have no personal experience with them, just my experience in SE Asia. Good luck and remember, this is a global economy and education is very high priced in the US. You can get a great education elsewhere that will count in the US.
Where did you study? I would've loved to have the opportunity to study abroad. Still waiting on my University to send people to China. Hopefully next year.

I studied medicine in Manila, the Philippines. I graduate later this month. In the US right now doing some US experience work. We had a couple of people from Mainland China in my class....some from Taiwan, Iran, Europe, all over really.....was a great experience and had bad times but a lot of good times.
Which school in Manila, if that's not too much to ask? :>

hmmmm.....maybe after I graduate...lol but there are several schools there. If I was going to go again I would choose a school outside of Manila. Baguio, Cebu, Damaguette.....Maybe Angeles......there are reasons that are important to me, now that I understand more about the culture and the country. Cost being a big one......much less in the "provinces".

In Asia things are a bit different than here in the US. No need to upset someone because they do not understand the meaning of what you are saying. When in a different culture you try and stay sensitive to that culture. Their experiences are not yours and their view of the world is much different. Not bad....just different.

I actually enrolled in a foreign university. You need a four year undergrad degree, take what the Philippines call the NMAT,....best describe it as a basic skills test.....all day..........and the rest is just ........study...... Feel free to ask me more questions if that was not clear enough! :)

Another interesting aspect is you can get a 4 year nursing degree there....many of the students had and then decided to work on their doctorate. Not to bore people....but if you are a highschool graduate there are many fine programs that you can avail yourselves of, accounting, math, teaching, science etc........
